### Script for Analysis of seqFISH mouse hippocampus dataset for "Are low-variance Principal Components of single-cell omics data biologically meaningful, or just noise?"
### Data source:
### Shah et al. 2016
### https://www.cell.com/neuron/fulltext/S0896-6273(16)30702-4
### PCA on the 214 barcoded genes; spatial correlation by nearest-neighbour rank within each field of view; exponential decay fits; predicted noise fraction per PC; Figure 2 panels
### Inputs: mmc6.xlsx 
### Outputs panels for figure 2. 



```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
### Load libraries
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggrepel)
library(cowplot)
library("patchwork")
library(ggnewscale)
```


```{r}
### Functions

### Calculate spatial correlation by nearest-neighbour rank
### For each PC, correlate each cell's PC score with the score of its
### 1st, 2nd, ..., kth nearest neighbour.
### Returns a matrix with PCs as rows and neighbour ranks as columns.
### pearson correlation computed across all cells from all fields of view pooled
pc_correlation <- function(x_scores, y_scores_full, neighbour_pairs) {
  num_pcs <- ncol(x_scores); k <- ncol(neighbour_pairs)
  cor_matrix <- matrix(NA, num_pcs, k,
    dimnames = list(colnames(x_scores), paste0("Neighbor", 1:k)))
  for (p in 1:num_pcs) {
    x <- x_scores[, p]
    for (c in 1:k) {
      y <- y_scores_full[neighbour_pairs[, c], p]
      cor_matrix[p, c] <- cor(x, y, use = "complete.obs")
    }
  }
  cor_matrix
}

### Run PCA and calculate neighbour-rank spatial correlations
### PCA is performed after centering and scaling each gene.
### Returns the PCA object and the spatial correlation matrix
run_pc_spatial <- function(mat, nn_idx) {
  pca <- prcomp(mat, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
  scores <- as.matrix(pca$x)
  cors <- pc_correlation(scores, scores, nn_idx)
  list(pca = pca, cor = cors)
}

### Fit exponential spatial-decay curves
# Fit C(d) = A * exp(-d / L), where A is the correlation amplitude and L is the length scale

fit_exponential_decay <- function(dist, corr) {
  df_fit <- data.frame(d = dist, corr = as.numeric(corr)) %>%
    filter(is.finite(corr), is.finite(d))
  if (nrow(df_fit) < 10) return(c(A=NA, lambda=NA, A_se=NA, lambda_se=NA))
#### Starting value for L: the distance at which the correlation is closest to 1/e of its maximum, with a minimum of 5 µm
  corr_thresh <- max(df_fit$corr) / exp(1)
  L_start <- df_fit$d[which.min(abs(df_fit$corr - corr_thresh))]
  L_start <- max(L_start, 5)
  
  fit <- tryCatch(
    nls(corr ~ A * exp(-d / L), data = df_fit,
      ### Initialize A as the maximum observed correlation.  
        start = list(A = max(df_fit$corr), L = L_start),
        lower = c(A = -1, L = min(df_fit$d)),
        upper = c(A = 1, L = max(df_fit$d)),
        algorithm = "port"),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  
  # fallback if first attempt fails
  if (is.null(fit)) {
    fit <- tryCatch(
      nls(corr ~ A * exp(-d / L), data = df_fit,
          start = list(A = 0.01, L = 100),
          lower = c(A = -1, L = min(df_fit$d)),
          upper = c(A = 1, L = max(df_fit$d)),
          algorithm = "port"),
      error = function(e) NULL)
  }
    ### return outputs
  if (is.null(fit)) return(c(A=NA, lambda=NA, A_se=NA, lambda_se=NA))
  sm <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  c(A = sm["A","Estimate"], lambda = sm["L","Estimate"],
    A_se = sm["A","Std. Error"], lambda_se = sm["L","Std. Error"])
}
```

### SeqFISH mouse hippocampus dataset from Shah et al. 2016
### The source file contains 249 measured genes across 21 fields of view:
### 214 barcoded seqFISH genes followed by 35 serial smHCR genes.
### PCA and subsequent analyses use the 214 barcoded genes.

### 1. Data loading
```{r}

### load in gene counts 
counts <- suppressMessages(read_excel("Data/mmc6.xlsx", sheet = "Hippocampus Counts", col_names = FALSE))

### load in centroids of cells 
centroids <- suppressMessages(read_excel("Data/mmc6.xlsx", sheet = "Centroids", col_names = FALSE))

### Load the field-of-view (FOV) label of each cell
field_vec <- suppressMessages(read_excel("Data/mmc6.xlsx", sheet = "Field Vector", col_names = FALSE))

### Strip quote marks from the gene names (first column) and use them as row names; transpose so that rows are cells and columns are genes. Centroids are X, Y, Z in pixels
counts <- as.data.frame(counts) %>% mutate(...1 = str_remove_all(...1, "'"))
genenames <- counts$...1
rownames(counts) <- genenames
counts <- counts %>% select(-...1)
colnames(counts) <- 1:ncol(counts)
counts_t <- as.data.frame(t(counts))

colnames(centroids) <- c("X", "Y", "Z")
fov <- t(field_vec)

##combine into one DF
Full_DF <- cbind(counts_t, centroids, fov)

markers <- counts_t

### 214 barcoded by seqFISH, 35 serial smHCR (per Shah et al. 2016 methods)
### Keep only the 214 barcoded genes for PCA, because the serial smHCR genes differ in noise and expression level
### File lists the 214 barcoded genes first and the 35 serial genes last
barcoded_genes <- head(colnames(markers), 214)


```

### 2. Nearest neighbours within each field of view
```{r}
### Take the total number of cells in the FOV with the fewest cells - 1 and set that as the number of NN to take
### selected so every cell in each fov has the same number of neighbours and that we do not take more NN than exist
k_nn <- min(table(Full_DF$fov)) - 1
cat("k =", k_nn, "\n")


#### X and Y are within FOV, add an offset so nearest neighbours are restricted to the same FOV and will not cross over to other FOVs
Full_DF_pool <- Full_DF %>%
  mutate(
    X_shifted = X + as.integer(factor(fov)) * 10000,
    Y_shifted = Y + as.integer(factor(fov)) * 10000
  )

### Run NN on the shifted coords, so each cells NN are only within FOV
knn_pool <- RANN::nn2(
  data  = as.matrix(Full_DF_pool[, c("X_shifted", "Y_shifted")]),
  query = as.matrix(Full_DF_pool[, c("X_shifted", "Y_shifted")]),
  k = k_nn + 1
)
###Get the index of each cell and their K NN, dropping the first NN (self)
nn_idx <- knn_pool$nn.idx[, -1, drop = FALSE]

### Mean distance to the n-th nearest neighbour, averaged over all cells (self excluded)
mean_d <- colMeans(knn_pool$nn.dists[, -1, drop = FALSE])

# Confirm no cross-FOV neighbors 
focal_fov <- Full_DF_pool$fov
nbr_fov   <- matrix(focal_fov[nn_idx], nrow = nrow(nn_idx), ncol = ncol(nn_idx))
cat("Cross-FOV neighbor pairs:", sum(nbr_fov != focal_fov), "\n")



### convert from pixel to um. Each field of view is 216 × 216 µm, imaged at 1024 × 1024 pixels

mean_d_um <- mean_d * (216/1024)
```

### 3. PCA and spatial correlation by nearest-neighbour rank

```{r}
### apply log(1 + count) transform to markers 
markers_log <- log1p(markers)

### Perform PCA on the 214 barcoded genes and calculate spatial correlations as a function of nearest-neighbour rank
res_barcoded <- run_pc_spatial(markers_log[, barcoded_genes], nn_idx)

var_explained_barcoded = res_barcoded$pca$sdev^2 / sum(res_barcoded$pca$sdev^2)

```



### 4. Exponential fits to the correlation curves 
```{r}
### spatial correlation is expected to decay with  distance if a PC captures real tissue structure
### Model this decay as A·exp(−d/L), where A is the amplitude and L is the length scale
cor_br <- res_barcoded$cor

#### For each PC, fit A·exp(−d/L) to its correlation versus mean neighbour distance (µm)
fit_params <- as.data.frame(t(sapply(rownames(cor_br), function(pc) {
  fit_exponential_decay(mean_d_um, cor_br[pc, ])
})))

fit_params$PC <- seq_len(nrow(fit_params))

```

### 5. Plot correlation curves with exponential fits (Fig 2. C)
```{r}

pcs_to_show <- c("PC1", "PC5", "PC10", "PC20", "PC50", "PC100")

### Observed correlation versus mean neighbour distance for the PCs shown
decay_df <- bind_rows(lapply(pcs_to_show, function(pc) {
  data.frame(
    PC     = pc,
    PC_num = as.numeric(sub("PC", "", pc)),
    dist   = mean_d_um,
    cor    = as.numeric(cor_br[pc, ])
  )
}))

### Fitted curve A·exp(−d/L) for each PC shown, evaluated at 200 evenly spaced distances
fit_df <- bind_rows(lapply(pcs_to_show, function(pc) {
  co <- fit_exponential_decay(mean_d_um, cor_br[pc, ])
  if (!all(is.finite(co))) return(NULL)
  d_seq <- seq(min(mean_d_um), max(mean_d_um), length.out = 200)
  data.frame(
    PC     = pc,
    PC_num = as.numeric(sub("PC", "", pc)),
    dist   = d_seq,
    cor    = co["A"] * exp(-d_seq / co["lambda"])
  )
}))




p <- ggplot(decay_df, aes(x = dist, y = cor, group = PC, colour = PC_num)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.45) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(
    name   = "PC #",
    trans  = "log10",
    breaks = as.numeric(sub("PC", "", pcs_to_show))
  ) +
  new_scale_colour() +
  geom_line(
    data = fit_df,
    aes(x = dist, y = cor, group = PC, colour = "Exponential fit"),
    linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.35
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL, values = c("Exponential fit" = "red")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  labs(x = "Mean distance (µm)", y = "Correlation") +
   theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "gray90", linetype = "solid",linewidth = 0.12),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray80", linetype = "solid",linewidth = 0.23)
  ) 
print(p) 


seqfish_curve_legend <- get_legend(p)
seqfish_curve_no_legend <- p + theme(legend.position = "none")
ggsave("Data/Fig_seqfish_curve_legend.svg", plot = seqfish_curve_legend,
       width = 1, height = 3, units = "in",
       dpi = 300) 

ggsave("Data/Fig_seqfish_curve.svg", plot = seqfish_curve_no_legend,
       width = 3, height = 2, units = "in",
       dpi = 300)

```





### 6. Plot fitted spatial-decay parameters (Fig 2. D)
```{r}

fit_plot_all <- fit_params %>%
  filter(!is.na(A), !is.na(lambda))



### add labels to pcs up to 15
fit_plot_all <- fit_plot_all %>% 
  mutate(under_15 = ifelse(PC <= 15,paste0("PC",PC),""))

### make plot of parameters 

seqfish_param<- ggplot(fit_plot_all, aes(x = lambda, y = A, color = PC)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(
    name = "PC #",
    trans = "log10",
    breaks = c(1, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200)
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  labs(
    x = expression("L (µm)"),
    y = expression(A),
  ) +
   geom_text_repel(aes(label = under_15)) +
   theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "gray90", linetype = "solid",linewidth = 0.12),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray80", linetype = "solid",linewidth = 0.23)
  ) 

print(seqfish_param)

parm_legend <- get_legend(seqfish_param)


seqfish_param_no_legend <- seqfish_param + theme(legend.position = "none")



ggsave("Data/Fig_seqfish_param_legend.svg", plot = parm_legend,
       width = 2, height = 3, units = "in",
       dpi = 300)  

ggsave("Data/Fig_seqfish_param.svg", plot = seqfish_param_no_legend,
       width = 3, height = 2, units = "in",
       dpi = 300)  

```




### 7. Predicted noise fraction per PC (Fig 2. A)

```{r}

### get the PCA object
pca_br <- res_barcoded$pca 
### Assumed values of r, the correlation between a gene's measured and true expression: 0.20 to 0.80 in steps of 0.05.
r_vals <- round(seq(0.2, 0.8, by = 0.05), 2)

### squared loadings: the weight of each gene's noise variance in each PC
loadings_sq <- pca_br$rotation^2
### Total variance of each PC
pc_total    <- pca_br$sdev^2
### Number of genes in the PCA
n_genes     <- nrow(pca_br$rotation)

###  Propagate gene-level noise variance into PC-level noise variance
### Genes are scaled to unit variance, so a gene measured with correlation r to its true expression has noise variance 1 − r²
noise_df <- purrr::map_dfr(r_vals, function(r_i) {
  gene_noise <- rep(1 - r_i^2, n_genes)
  ### Assumes measurement noise is independent across genes, so noise variances add through the squared loadings.
  pc_noise   <- colSums(loadings_sq * gene_noise)
  ### Noise fraction = predicted PC noise variance / total PC variance, with the same r assumed for every gene
  data.frame(PC = seq_along(pc_total), noise_fraction = pc_noise / pc_total, r = r_i)
})


seq_fish_noise <- ggplot(noise_df, aes(PC, noise_fraction, color = r, group = r)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  ### Green line: fraction of total variance explained by each PC, for comparison with the predicted noise fractions.
    geom_line(data = data.frame(PC = seq_along(var_explained_barcoded),
                              ve = var_explained_barcoded),
            aes(PC, ve, linetype = "Total variance"), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            colour = "darkgreen", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_linetype_manual(name = NULL, values = c("Total variance" = "solid")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.8, linetype = "dotted", color = "red") +
  annotate("text", x = 200, y = 0.8, label = "80% noise", hjust = 8.5, vjust = 2, size = 3.2, color = "red") +
   scale_x_log10(
    breaks = scales::log_breaks(n = 5),
    minor_breaks = scales::minor_breaks_n(10),
    labels = scales::label_log()
  ) +
   scale_y_log10(
    breaks = scales::log_breaks(n = 5),
    minor_breaks = scales::minor_breaks_n(10),
    labels = scales::label_log()
  ) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Assumed r", option = "turbo") +
   theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "gray90", linetype = "solid",linewidth = 0.12),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray80", linetype = "solid",linewidth = 0.23)
  ) +
  labs(x = "PC", y = "Proportion of variance")


### Number of PCs with predicted noise fraction below 80%, for each assumed r
noise_df %>% group_by(r) %>% summarise(n_PCs_below_80 = sum(noise_fraction < 0.8)) %>% print()

print(seq_fish_noise)
seq_fish_noise_legend <- get_legend(seq_fish_noise)

seq_fish_noise_no_legend <- seq_fish_noise + theme(legend.position = "none")


ggsave("Data/Fig_seqfish_noise_legend.svg", plot = seq_fish_noise_legend,
       width = 1, height = 3, units = "in",
       dpi = 300)  

ggsave("Data/Fig_seqfish_noise.svg", plot = seq_fish_noise_no_legend,
       width = 3, height = 2, units = "in",
       dpi = 300)  
```

### 8. Maps of two fields of view coloured by PC score (Fig 2. B)

```{r}

### FOVs 52 and 53; PCs 1, 8 and 100
scores_br <- pca_br$x
fov_ids <- c(52, 53)
pcs_map <- c("PC1", "PC8", "PC100")
### set colour scale 
cols <- colorRampPalette(c("#FFFFFF", "#08306B"))(100)

Full_DF_for_plot <- Full_DF
### convert to um
Full_DF_for_plot$X_um <- Full_DF$X * (216/1024)

Full_DF_for_plot$Y_um <- Full_DF$Y* (216/1024)

## make the plot
 plist <- list()
 store <-1 
for (fov_id in fov_ids) {
  for (pc in pcs_map) {
    idx <- which(Full_DF_for_plot$fov == fov_id)
    plot_df <- Full_DF_for_plot[idx,]
    vals <- scores_br[idx, pc]
    ### scores are standardised within each FOV and clipped at ±2 SD for display 
    vals_scaled <- (vals - mean(vals)) / sd(vals)
    vals_clamped <- pmax(pmin(vals_scaled, 2), -2)
    plot_df$vals_clamped <- vals_clamped

  p <- ggplot(plot_df,aes(X_um,Y_um,colour=vals_clamped))+
         geom_point() +
     scale_colour_gradientn(colours = cols, limits = c(-2, 2),name = "PC score (SD)",
    guide = guide_colourbar(
    direction = "vertical",
    barheight = unit(4, "cm"),
    barwidth  = unit(0.3, "cm"),
    ticks.colour = "white",
    frame.colour = "white",
    title.position = "right"
  )) +
       theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = 'black'), 
             panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
             panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
             panel.border = element_rect(color = "red"),
             axis.text = element_blank(),
             axis.ticks = element_blank(),
             axis.title = element_blank(),
             plot.margin=unit(c(0.25,0,0.25,0), 'cm'),
             plot.background = element_rect(fill = "black", colour = NA),
             plot.title = element_text(colour = "white",size = 10),
               legend.text = element_text(colour = "white"),
               legend.box.spacing = unit(0.1, "cm"),
  legend.title = element_text(colour = "white",angle=270),
  legend.background = element_rect(fill = "black", colour = NA),
  legend.key = element_rect(fill = "black", colour = NA)
             ) + 
    labs(title = (paste(pc))) +
    coord_fixed(
  xlim = c(-10, 226),
  ylim = c(-10, 226),
  expand = FALSE
) 
  
     p<- p + annotate("segment", x = 10, xend = 60, y = 10, yend = 10, colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +annotate("text", x = 35, y = 18, label = "50 µm", colour = "white", size = 3)
     
  plist[[store]] <- p 
  store <- store + 1 
    
  
  }
}




 final_plot <- (
  (plist[[1]] | plist[[2]] | plist[[3]]) /
  (plist[[4]] | plist[[5]] | plist[[6]])
) +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(
    theme = theme(
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "black", colour = NA)
    )
  ) &
  theme(
    legend.position = "none"
  )



legend_grob <- get_legend(
  plist[[1]] +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
      legend.box.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
    )
)

legend_plot <- ggdraw(legend_grob) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "black", colour = NA)
  )
ggsave(
  "Data/PC_score_legend.svg",
  plot = legend_plot,
  width = 1.2,
  height = 2.4,
  bg = "black"
)



ggsave("Data/Fig_seqfish_map.svg", plot = final_plot,
       width = 3, height = 3, units = "in",
       dpi = 300)  


```
### 9. Variance of PCs 4-13 relative to PCs 1-3 and PCs > 30

```{r}
### Mean variance per PC in each group; ratios quoted in the text (~46-fold and ~2-fold)
ev <- pca_br$sdev^2
mean(ev[1:3]) / mean(ev[4:13])       # how many times lower than PCs 1-3
mean(ev[4:13]) / mean(ev[31:214])    # how many times higher than PCs > 30
```
